draft.title: Surface area and volume of a sphere
card: A sphere is a perfectly round solid. Every point on its surface is the same distance, the radius \(r\), from the centre.
Surface area
\(SA = 4\pi r^{2}\). This is four times the area of a circle with the same radius.
Volume
\(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\). The radius is cubed, not squared, because volume is measured in cubic units.
Example

A ball has radius 3 cm. \(SA = 4 \times \pi \times 3^{2} = 36\pi\), which is about \(113.1\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\). \(V = \frac{4}{3} \times \pi \times 3^{3} = 36\pi\), which is about \(113.1\) \(\text{cm}^{3}\).
draft.remember: Surface area uses \(r^{2}\) with 4. Volume uses \(r^{3}\) with \(\frac{4}{3}\).

a.q: Which pair of formulas gives the surface area and the volume of a sphere with radius \(r\)?
a.why: Surface area is measured in square units, so it uses \(r^{2}\), and volume uses \(r^{3}\). The swapped pair is tempting, but it puts the cube on the area.
a.clue: Area uses a square, volume uses a cube.

b.q: A spherical water tank at a farm in Wodonga has radius 2 m. What is its volume, to the nearest cubic metre?
b.why: \(V = \frac{4}{3} \times \pi \times 2^{3} = \frac{32\pi}{3}\), which is about 33.5, so 34 cubic metres. The value 50 is the surface area \(4\pi \times 2^{2}\), which is the wrong formula. The value 101 comes from using \(r = 4\) by mistake.

problems.detail: Why (b) says 101 comes from using r = 4 by mistake, but with r = 4 the volume is about 268 m³. 101 comes from leaving out the 1/3: 4π × 2³ = 32π ≈ 100.5.

The worked example uses r = 3, where the surface area and volume share the same number (36π ≈ 113.1). This is the one radius where they match, and students may take it to mean surface area and volume are equal or interchangeable. A different radius would avoid the coincidence.
